turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come through, Mr Perrin. I've done your observations out in the waiting room. Blood pressure 128 over 76, pulse 102, temperature 36.9.

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Right, thanks. Um, I'll try not to ramble, but we were at my niece's wedding on Saturday, reception at the golf club, speeches went on forever, and since Sunday morning I've basically lived in the loo.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'm Janet, his wife. I was at the same do. He's been really rough, and a few others have come down with it, his brother texted this morning.
[SEG0004] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, one second, the screen's gone blank again. Right. Can you start again from when it actually began? I only caught the wedding bit.

[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, of course. Saturday was a lovely day, he had the chicken and I had the prawns to start, and then Sunday, about six in the morning, I woke up and had to dash. Diarrhoea, proper watery, and I was sick as well.
[SEG0006] person_4 (DOCTOR): How long has that been going on? Sorry, your record is still loading.

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): It's been five days... no, hang on, that's not right. Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, and today's Wednesday, so three days. I always stick an extra day on when I'm counting, sorry.
[SEG0008] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, three days. He was fine all through the meal on Saturday evening. Ate plenty, unfortunately.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): And other people from the wedding are ill, you said?

[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): His brother Dave, Dave's wife, and at least two from the top table, according to the bride's mum on the family WhatsApp. Same sort of thing, sickness and the runs. I felt a bit queasy Sunday night but I was fine by Monday.

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): I haven't kept a chart, I'm not that organised, but yesterday I thought I'd been twelve times, no, I counted properly before bed and it was eight. Eight times yesterday. Today I've already been three times and it's only half ten.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Eight. Say that once more, I was typing in the wrong box.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Eight bowel movements yesterday, all watery, no form to them at all. And three already this morning. There's cramping low down beforehand, then it just rushes through.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any blood in the stool, or black stools?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No blood. I did look, because Dave said his had a bit of blood and I panicked, but mine is just brown water, if that's not too much information. No black either.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Is the vomiting still going on?

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): I was sick six times on Sunday... no, four. Four times Sunday, once early Monday, and nothing since. I still feel a bit sick if I smell food, but I'm not actually being sick now.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He won't eat. Sips of water and that's about it. And he's not weeing much, he said this morning it was quite dark.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or shivers?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't think so. I felt a bit hot under the duvet Sunday night but I never took my temperature, and I haven't felt feverish since. No shivers really.
[SEG0021] person_1 (NURSE): Temperature was 36.9, so nothing raised. Can I just check the loperamide, because the chemist note on the screen says loperamide 2 milligrams twice a day?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): That's not what I've been doing. The capsules are 2 milligrams, yes, but I've been taking two of them each time.
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And not twice. He's been taking them four times a day since Monday. The pharmacist told him not to if it might be a bug, and he ignored her.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the screen jumped. What dose did you just read out?
[SEG0025] person_1 (NURSE): The note says 2 milligrams twice daily. That's all that's written down.

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Well the note's wrong then. Two capsules, so 4 milligrams, four times a day. I know you're not meant to, the lady in Boots said leave it alone with a tummy bug, but I had to log on for work Monday so I took it anyway.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): Please stop the loperamide. With this many people ill after the same meal I don't want you slowing your gut down. It can just hold onto whatever this is.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Even if I'm up and down all night? I'll stop if you say so. The cramps are grim, though, and it did take the edge off for an hour or two.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, stop it. Fluids are the useful bit, not that. Any other regular medicines?

[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Omeprazole, 20 milligrams, once in the morning, for the reflux. I've been on that years. I didn't take it this morning because I was throwing... well, I wasn't throwing up, I just couldn't face the tablet, so I missed today's.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): That's fine, restart it tomorrow if you can keep it down. Any allergies to medicines, or anything else?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing. I've had penicillin before, no problem, and no food allergies that I know of. Janet's the one with the hay fever, not me.

[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good. Let me have a quick look. Mouth's a bit dry, tongue's dry. Tummy's soft, a little tender across the lower part, no guarding. You're not markedly dehydrated, but you are on the dry side.
[SEG0034] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Is the pulse being that fast part of it? 102 seemed high for him, he's usually down in the sixties.

[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes, that fits with being a bit dry. Heart rate 102, and the blood pressure was fine at 128 over 76. I think this is food poisoning, a straightforward gastroenteritis from the wedding meal. Provisional, obviously, I can't prove which bug.

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Do I need antibiotics? Dave said his GP gave him something. I don't want tablets for the sake of it, but if everyone else is on them I don't want to be the one who gets worse.

[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): No antibiotics just now. Most of these settle on their own. What I do want is fluids, little and often, oral rehydration salts from the chemist, Dioralyte or whatever they have. Water is alright but the salts are better, so sip, don't gulp.

[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): How much, roughly? I tend to overdo instructions, like is it a glass an hour or more than that? And can I have tea? I really want a cup of tea, milk no sugar, that's my usual.

[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Tea is fine if it stays down. Aim for sips through the day until you're weeing a proper amount and it's paler. If you're dizzy when you stand, you stop weeing, you see blood, or you can't keep any fluid down at all, come straight back, or go to A&E if you can't keep fluids down.
[SEG0040] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): What about a stool sample? Dave said they asked him for one.
[SEG0041] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not today. If it's not settling in three days, or if you see blood, then we'll send a stool sample. No need while he's otherwise alright.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): And work? I'm a bookkeeper, I work from the spare room, so I'm not with the public, but I feel guilty not logging on. I did half an hour yesterday and had to stop.
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): Stay off until the diarrhoea has been gone a full 48 hours. Even from home, you need the rest, and you don't want to be dashing mid-spreadsheet.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Forty-eight hours after it stops. Right. And I'll stop the Imodium, the loperamide I mean. Sorry, I keep using the brand name.
[SEG0045] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll pick up the Dioralyte on the way home. Should we book something to come back?

[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): If it's not better in three days, book back in with me. Otherwise you don't need a routine appointment. The screen's behaving now, I'll write the note. Alright, take care.

features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

omissions.text: Loperamide dosing is recorded wrongly/incompletely: patient/family said he has been taking two 2 mg capsules (4 mg) four times a day since Monday, despite pharmacist advice not to take it if it might be an infectious diarrhoeal illness.
Patient missed today's omeprazole dose because he could not face the tablet due to illness.
Other attendees from the wedding were also unwell with similar symptoms: brother Dave, Dave's wife, and at least two from the top table; wife also felt queasy Sunday night but recovered by Monday.
Diarrhoea began at about 6 am on Sunday.
Stools described as brown watery stool with no form at all.
Cramping occurs low down beforehand, then diarrhoea 'rushes through'.
Patient reported feeling a bit hot under the duvet on Sunday night but did not measure temperature, and has not felt feverish since.
Allergy history detail omitted: patient specifically reported having had penicillin before with no problem, and no known food allergies.
Doctor advised no antibiotics at this stage because most cases settle on their own.
Safety-net advice included going to A&E if unable to keep fluids down at all.
No routine follow-up needed if improving/otherwise alright.
